concepts.def: Source replenished naturally on human timescales.
Finite resource depleted faster than it forms.
Coal, oil and gas from ancient buried organisms.
Electricity from photovoltaic cells or solar thermal.
Kinetic energy of wind turning turbine blades.
Energy from fission of uranium; low-carbon but not renewable.

walkthroughs.body_html: Renewable sources include solar (PV and thermal), wind (onshore and offshore), hydroelectric (dams and run-of-river), geothermal (Earth's heat), biomass (organic matter combustion) and tidal (predictable lunar-driven flows). They are continually replenished and produce little or no direct CO2, though land use and materials still have impacts.

Coal, oil and natural gas formed over millions of years from buried organisms. Burning them releases CO2 and pollutants. Nuclear fission of uranium is low-carbon but uranium is finite and waste is radioactive for millennia. Non-renewables currently supply roughly 80 percent of global primary energy.

Sustainability means meeting current needs without compromising future generations. For energy this requires shifting from finite fossil sources to renewables, improving efficiency, reducing demand and managing impacts on land, water and biodiversity. The UN Sustainable Development Goal 7 targets affordable clean energy for all.
